title: Map Render Contract
description: Schema + rules for the standalone render skill. The render skill draws an emoji grid of the CURRENT situation from campaign_state.map, the active act's location/positions, and the avatar-registry. It is DISPLAY-ONLY: it never resolves an encounter and never sets a loop flag. It is invoked as a render STEP by spatial loops (combat, scene/exploration, travel, positional challenge) and on the player's explicit request.

map_state_schema.description: Shape of the `map` object stored in campaign_state.json. Regenerated/updated by the render skill each render.

frame.description: [width, height] in tiles. Default 20x10. May shrink (e.g. [12,8] for a cramped corridor) or grow as needed; keep width so the row fits the terminal (~2 columns per emoji).

scene.description: Short label of what is being rendered (e.g. 'Foundry chokepoint').

terrain_key.description: Environment archetype used to pick default tiles: 'dungeon' | 'cavern' | 'town' | 'forest' | 'road' | 'interior' | 'wilderness'. Derived from the act's location.environment.

id.description: character_id for PCs, or a unique enemy id like 'orc-1'.

monster_id.description: For enemies: the stat-block id used for avatar lookup.

category.description: Fallback creature category if monster_id has no explicit avatar.

down.description: true if unconscious/dead (render dimmed or as 💀).

features.description: Static terrain features placed on the grid.

terrain.description: A key in avatar-registry.terrain (wall, water, door, loot, stairs_down, ...).

generation_rules.layout_source: OPTION A (state-tracked, generated). On first render of a scene, generate the grid from the act file: use location.environment -> terrain_key for the base tile, walls around the border, and place enemy tokens from the encounter `position` strings (e.g. 'behind the arrow slits' -> near a wall edge; 'on the dais' -> far side). Place the party at the entrance. Persist the result to campaign_state.map.
generation_rules.movement: On later renders, move tokens per what happened (combat movement, travel). Update campaign_state.map.tokens x/y — do NOT regenerate the whole layout unless the scene changes.
generation_rules.anti_drift: Terrain and creatures come from the act file + tracked state — do not invent creatures. Enemy avatars resolve via avatar-registry (monster_id -> category fallback).
generation_rules.frame_default: 20x10 unless the scene is clearly smaller/larger; never exceed a width that wraps the terminal.

render_rules.one_emoji_per_tile: Each tile renders exactly one full-width emoji: the topmost token if present, else its terrain feature, else the base floor tile. No variation-selector glyphs (they skew columns).
render_rules.no_coordinates: Do NOT print row numbers or column letters around the grid (per design).
render_rules.legend: Print a one-line legend under the grid listing only the tokens/terrain actually shown (party avatars + which enemies + key terrain).
render_rules.placement: The map renders ABOVE the action-prompt menu, as part of the same view.
render_rules.output_format: Follows .claude/skills/action-prompt/SKILL.md — narration, then the map, then the ACTIONS block.

invocation.not_a_dispatch_loop: render has NO *.active flag and is NEVER dispatched by state-evaluation-contract. It does not compete in the one-flag mutual-exclusion invariant.
invocation.called_by: Invoked as a render step by spatial loops (combat every round; scene/exploration on entering a location; travel on arrival/encounter; positional challenge) and on explicit player request ('show map' / 'map').
invocation.returns: Nothing to resolve — it emits the drawn grid + legend and returns control to the calling loop.
